site.acme.failed: Couldn’t issue a certificate for {name}. Check that the A record of the domain points to this server and that port 80 is open from outside (the hosting provider’s firewall).
site.acme.limit_dup: Let’s Encrypt temporarily does not issue certificates for {name} (limit).
site.acme.limit_failed: Let’s Encrypt temporarily does not check {name}: there were too many failed checks (limit). You can try again {when}. Before that check the A record of the domain and port 80 from outside.
site.acme.limit_generic: Let’s Encrypt temporarily does not issue certificates for {name} (limit): after failed checks — about an hour, after five certificates in a week — up to a week. The exact time is in /var/log/letsencrypt/letsencrypt.log (the line “retry after”).
site.acme.limit_when: Let’s Encrypt temporarily does not issue certificates for {name} (limit). You can try again {when}.
site.acme.log_certbot: SITE: installed the certbot package (for the Let’s Encrypt certificate)
site.acme.net: The server couldn’t reach Let’s Encrypt: the outgoing connection broke. The domain and port 80 are not the cause — it is the network of the server or of the hosting provider. Try again in a few minutes; if it still fails, ask the hosting provider about outgoing connections to port 443.
site.acme.other_name: The server is fine — this is a Let’s Encrypt limit: at most five identical certificates for one name a week. Don’t want to wait — take another name (for example the subdomain vpn2.{name}): a new name has its own limit, it only needs an A record pointing to this server.
site.acme.port80: Port 80/tcp on the server is used by another program (a web server, for example), and certbot couldn’t take it for the Let’s Encrypt check. Free port 80 and try again; Kaskad does not stop services that are not its own.
site.consumers.log_handed: SITE: certificate {domain} (until {until}) handed to its consumers: {names}
site.consumers.log_handed_panel: SITE: certificate {domain} (until {until}) handed to its consumers: the panel takes it itself
site.consumers.log_hy2_failed: SITE: Hysteria2 did not switch to the other certificate: {error}
site.consumers.no_files: No certificate files in {path} — issue it: kaskadctl site cert issue
site.consumers.other_names: The certificate in {path} is not for {domain} (it has: {names}) — not copying it.
site.consumers.pair: Couldn’t prepare the certificate and key pair: {error}
site.consumers.unreadable: The certificate in {path} cannot be read: {error}
site.dns.aaaa: {name} has an AAAA record (IPv6) that does not point to this server: {aaaa}. Let’s Encrypt tries IPv6 first and may not issue the certificate — delete this record or point it to the IPv6 of this server.
site.dns.cloudflare: Proxying seems to be on for {name} in Cloudflare (the orange cloud): Cloudflare’s addresses are seen instead of the server’s. For the VPN and the certificate switch the record to “DNS only” (the gray cloud).
site.dns.elsewhere: {name} points to {a}, while this server’s addresses are {own}: the Let’s Encrypt check will fail. Fix the A record in the DNS settings of the domain.
site.dns.no_own: Couldn’t find the public address of this server — nothing to compare the A records of {name} with.
site.dns.none: {name} has no A record — the Let’s Encrypt check will fail. In the DNS settings of the domain add an A record with the value {own} (the address of this server). A record starts working in a few minutes, sometimes in an hour.
site.dns.partial: {name} also points to addresses of other servers: {foreign}. Connections by the domain will work only some of the time, and the Let’s Encrypt check may land there. Often it is a default record of the hosting provider or a record of an old server — delete it in the DNS panel and keep only the addresses of this server ({own}).
site.dns.unknown: DNS did not answer — couldn’t check the A records of {name}. Try again in a minute.
site.front.behind_no_tls: the site is behind xray, but xray holds 443 without TLS — the site on the domain won’t open: kaskadctl gw vless sync
site.front.chosen: Reality is your choice (the risks were accepted)
site.front.consent_bad: Reality is chosen, but the consent to its risks is missing — confirm it or switch to TLS
site.front.foreign_vhost: nginx has someone else’s site on 443
site.front.log_aside: GW vless: Reality (chosen) moves off 443 to port {port} — the server’s site takes 443
site.front.log_behind: SITE: nginx behind xray: the site answers through VLESS + TLS on 443 (socket {sock})
site.front.log_behind_no_tls: SITE: the site is behind xray, but xray holds 443 without TLS — the site on the domain won’t open: kaskadctl gw vless sync
site.front.log_not_rewritten: SITE: nginx was not rewritten for the gateway’s xray: {error}
site.front.log_room_error: GW vless: VLESS did not switch to TLS: {why}. VLESS stays on Reality, port {port}.
site.front.neighbour: another program’s nginx site is already set up on 443 ({names})
site.front.no_cert: no valid Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain}
site.front.no_copy: there is no copy of the domain certificate — issue it again (menu 19 → 2)
site.front.no_site: the site on the domain is off (the “site” mode)
site.front.no_vless: the VLESS protocol is not installed
site.front.no_vless_err: The VLESS protocol is not installed.
site.front.not_rewritten: the site on the domain was not rearranged for the gateway’s xray: {error}
site.front.panel_443: the panel’s open mode listens on 443 — move it to a port of its own: Settings → Panel
site.front.ready: TLS with your own domain can be turned on now — the VLESS links will have to be given out again
site.front.room_error: VLESS did not switch to TLS: {why}. VLESS stays on Reality, port {port}.
site.front.tls_error: VLESS did not switch to TLS: {why}
site.front.tls_failed: the last switch to TLS failed — try it again: kaskadctl gw vless mode tls
site.front.to_tls: VLESS switched to TLS with its own domain {domain} (port 443)
site.front.vless_off: the VLESS protocol or the gateway is off
site.front.xray_refused: the gateway’s xray did not accept the settings
site.model.bad_chars: The part “{label}” of the domain has invalid characters: only letters, digits and a hyphen (not first or last). {hint}
site.model.bad_email: The email must be an address like admin@example.com.
site.model.digits_tld: “{name}” is not a domain: its top-level zone is all digits. {hint}
site.model.domain_hint: A domain is a name like vpn.example.com (non-Latin letters work too).
site.model.empty_label: “{name}” has an empty part between dots. {hint}
site.model.idna: The part “{label}” of the domain cannot be converted to Latin letters (IDNA). {hint}
site.model.ip: “{name}” is an IP address, a domain is needed. {hint}
site.model.label_long: The part “{label}” of the domain is longer than 63 characters.
site.model.label_long_dns: The part “{label}” of the domain is longer than 63 characters (in its DNS form).
site.model.one_label: “{name}” is not a domain: it needs at least one dot. {hint}
site.model.too_long: The domain is longer than 253 characters.
site.model.wildcard: Let’s Encrypt does not issue a wildcard (*) domain over port 80 — enter a single name, for example vpn.example.com.
site.nginx.log_acme_reload: SITE: nginx was not reloaded after the temporary ACME vhost: {error}
site.nginx.log_enable_failed: SITE: nginx was not enabled to start with the system: {error}
site.nginx.log_installed: SITE: installed the nginx package (for the site)
site.nginx.log_test_after_remove: SITE: nginx -t failed after the Kaskad files were removed (someone else’s error): {error}
site.nginx.reload_failed: nginx did not reload its settings: {error}
site.ops.acme_extra_refused: nginx did not accept the Let’s Encrypt check for {domain}: {error}
site.ops.acme_refused: nginx did not accept the ACME settings of the domain: {error}. The previous files are back.
site.ops.bad_mode: The site mode is site or domain.
site.ops.behind_refused: nginx did not accept the site behind xray: {error}
site.ops.certbot_not_renewed: certbot did not renew the certificate
site.ops.default_page: the default nginx page answers on port 80 — the server gives itself away
site.ops.dns_waiting: DNS of {domain}: {state} — waiting more ({spent} s of {wait} passed)…
site.ops.email_later: Let’s Encrypt did not take the new email now — it will be given at the next issue.
site.ops.expiring: The certificate of {domain} expires in {n} day ({date}), couldn’t renew it: {why}|The certificate of {domain} expires in {n} days ({date}), couldn’t renew it: {why}
site.ops.foreign_hook: The certificate of {domain} already has its own deploy hook (another program set it) — keeping it; the daily Kaskad certificate watchdog will pick up the new certificate after a renewal.
site.ops.host_old: The client address stayed {old}: devices connect by it while its A record points here. To change it: kaskadctl gw host {domain} (or panel → “Gateway”).
site.ops.issued: The Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain} is issued.
site.ops.kept: The domain {domain} works as before — nothing changed on the server.
site.ops.kept_by_certbot: The certificate of {domain} is still valid — certbot kept it.
site.ops.log_80_not_freed: SITE: port 80 was not freed from Kaskad’s nginx: {error}
site.ops.log_acme_not_removed: SITE: the Kaskad ACME vhost was not removed: {error}
site.ops.log_cert_switch: SITE: certificate {domain} issued (until {until}) — switching the domain
site.ops.log_cleared: SITE: domain {domain} removed; consumers are on the self-signed certificate
site.ops.people_links_die: users’ links on the domain {domain} will stop opening — users need new links (users with links: {n})
site.ops.port_will_on: access by the port is off — it will be switched on first, under the secret address, or neither the panel nor users keep an address
site.ops.port_turned_on: access by the port was off — it is on again under the secret address: the panel and new links of users are on the port now (full address — «Panel address» or F1 in the SSH menu)
site.ops.port_off_change: access by the port is off — after the change the panel opens only on the new domain; if that does not open from outside, the only way in is the SSH tunnel
site.ops.log_port_back_on: SITE: domain {domain} is being removed while access by the port was off — switched on again so the panel and users keep an address
site.ops.log_cleared_kept: SITE: domain {domain} removed; consumers are on the self-signed certificate; the Let’s Encrypt certificate stays (autorenew = False)
site.ops.log_default_back: SITE: the default nginx page (sites-enabled/default) is back
site.ops.log_email_cleared: SITE: the email for Let’s Encrypt is removed
site.ops.log_email_set: SITE: the email for Let’s Encrypt is set
site.ops.log_has_cert: SITE: {domain} already has a Let’s Encrypt certificate ({days} days left) — taking it for the domain change
site.ops.log_issue: SITE: issuing a Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain}{staging}
site.ops.log_issue_change: SITE: issuing a Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain} (domain change from {old}; the old one works until the new one is ready)
site.ops.log_nginx_stopped: SITE: Kaskad’s nginx is stopped and disabled — port 80 is free for the certificate renewal
site.ops.log_path_rotated: SITE: the panel path on the site was replaced
site.ops.log_rb_done: SITE: rollback of the domain change: {domain} is back
site.ops.log_rb_failed: SITE: rollback of the domain change — {what} failed: {error}
site.ops.log_rb_partial: SITE: rollback of the domain change: {domain} is back (not all: {problems})
site.ops.log_removed: SITE: the domain and the certificate are removed from Kaskad (uninstall)
site.ops.log_settle_failed: SITE: Kaskad’s nginx was not stopped after the refusal: {error}
site.ops.log_site_off_standalone: SITE: the site is off; the domain and the certificate stay; port 80 for renewals: certbot --standalone
site.ops.log_site_off_webroot: SITE: the site is off; the domain and the certificate stay; port 80 for renewals: the Kaskad ACME vhost in nginx (webroot)
site.ops.log_site_on: SITE: the site on {domain} is on
site.ops.log_site_on_stub: SITE: the site on {domain} is on (a placeholder page: the templates did not download)
site.ops.log_switch_failed: SITE: the domain change {old} -> {domain} failed ({why}) — bringing {old} back
site.ops.log_tick_missing: SITE: certificate watchdog — no certificate files of {domain} in {path}
site.ops.log_tick_renewed: SITE: the certificate watchdog renewed the certificate of {domain} until {until}
site.ops.log_tpl_kept: SITE: the site template stays the same ({tid})
site.ops.log_use_off: SITE: {title} taken off the certificate of {domain}; devices with old settings: {n}
site.ops.log_use_on: SITE: {title} moved to the certificate of {domain}; devices with old settings: {n}
site.ops.log_vhost_refreshed: SITE: the nginx settings of the site are rewritten by this version’s template
site.ops.log_vhost_refused: SITE: the nginx settings of the site are not updated, the previous file is kept: {error}
site.ops.log_vless_not_switched: SITE: the VLESS mode was not switched: {error}
site.ops.need_domain: No domain set: kaskadctl site domain <name> (menu 19 → domain).
site.ops.neighbour: Another program’s nginx site is already set up on 443 ({names}). Keep the “domain” mode, move that site off port 443 or wait for the 4.1 “all on 443” mode.
site.ops.nginx_boot: nginx does not start with the system — after a reboot the site and the panel on the domain won’t open
site.ops.nginx_down: the site’s nginx is down — the site and the panel on {domain} don’t open
site.ops.nginx_down_noboot: the site’s nginx is down and does not start with the system — the site and the panel on {domain} don’t open
site.ops.nginx_install: Couldn’t install nginx for the site: {error}
site.ops.nginx_noboot: the site’s nginx does not start with the system — after a reboot the site and the panel on {domain} won’t open
site.ops.nginx_test_other: nginx did not accept the site settings: {error}. The previous file is back; check the configuration of the other nginx sites on this server.
site.ops.nginx_test_ours: nginx did not accept the site settings: {error}; the error is in the Kaskad site settings — tell the developer, the previous file is back.
site.ops.no_cert_renew: There is no Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain} — issue it first: kaskadctl site cert issue
site.ops.no_email: No email is set for Let’s Encrypt — its important emails (about a revoked certificate, changed terms) won’t reach you. Kaskad watches the expiry of the certificate itself: it renews it in advance and tells you in Telegram if the renewal hasn’t worked 21 days before the end.
site.ops.no_files: certbot finished successfully, but there are no certificate files for {domain} in {path}.
site.ops.off_no_domain: No domain set — nothing to switch to the domain mode from.
site.ops.off_refused: nginx did not accept the configuration without the site: {error}. The site file is back, nothing was switched off.
site.ops.over_staging: {domain} has a test certificate (staging) now — issuing a real one over it.
site.ops.panel_off: The panel is not open from the internet: no site on the domain and no access by the port.
site.ops.path_refused: nginx did not accept the new panel path: {error}. The old path stays.
site.ops.path_site_only: The secret address changes when the panel is open from the internet.
site.ops.port443: Port 443/tcp is in use: {who}. The site on the domain won’t be able to open. Keep the “domain” mode, move the protocol to another port or wait for the 4.1 “all on 443” mode; Kaskad does not stop someone else’s service.
site.ops.port80.issue: Port 80/tcp is in use: {who}. For the Let’s Encrypt check of the domain certbot has to take this port for a moment. Remove this forward or stop the service, then issue the certificate again. Kaskad does not stop services that are not its own.
site.ops.port80.renew: Port 80/tcp is in use: {who}. For the Let’s Encrypt check of the domain certbot has to take this port for a moment. Remove this forward or stop the service, then renew the certificate again. Kaskad does not stop services that are not its own.
site.ops.port80_not_ready: Port 80 is not ready for Let’s Encrypt: {error}
site.ops.port80_site: Port 80/tcp is in use: {who}. The site needs it to redirect http to https and to renew the Let’s Encrypt certificate. Remove this forward or stop the service, then try again. Kaskad does not stop services that are not its own.
site.ops.rb.no_cert: the certificate of {domain} is not on disk — issue it again
site.ops.rb.vless_links: VLESS — not on its old links
site.ops.reissue: {kinds}: {what} — settings issued before won’t connect. Reissue them (menu 17 → 2 → 1 or panel → “Users & devices”): {names}{more}.
site.ops.say.cert_wait: Let’s Encrypt checks {domain} over port 80; {old} keeps working meanwhile
site.ops.say.dns_wait: where the A record of {domain} points
site.ops.site_no_cert: The site needs a valid production Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain}. Issue it first: kaskadctl site cert issue (a --staging test one does not fit the site).
site.ops.site_no_domain: Set a domain for the site first: kaskadctl site domain <name>.
site.ops.staging: Let’s Encrypt test mode (--staging): browsers won’t accept such a certificate, but the limits are not spent.
site.ops.still_valid: The certificate of {domain} is valid for {days} more days — not reissuing it (Let’s Encrypt limits), only auto-renewal.
site.ops.switch_failed: The domain was not changed: {why}. The previous domain {old} is back — the site, the panel on the domain and VLESS work as before.
site.ops.switch_failed_partial: The domain was not changed: {why}. The previous domain {old} came back only partly: {problems}.
site.ops.tick_not_handed: The new certificate of {domain} was not handed to the panel and the protocols: {error}. Repeat item 19 → 2 in the SSH menu.
site.ops.tick_renewed_not_handed: The certificate of {domain} is renewed until {until}, but Kaskad did not hand it to the panel and the protocols: {error}. Repeat item 19 → 2 in the SSH menu.
site.ops.tpl_failed: The site template was not deployed: {error} The site is not on.
site.ops.tpl_failed_kept: The site template was not deployed: {error} The site is not on, everything stays as it was.
site.ops.use_kind: the protocol is sstp or ocserv
site.ops.use_no_cert: There is no Let’s Encrypt certificate for {domain} yet, or it expired — first kaskadctl site cert issue.
site.ops.use_not_installed: {title} is not installed yet — it will take the domain certificate when installed.
site.ops.use_staging: The certificate is a test one (staging): {title} clients won’t trust it.
site.ops.vhost_write_failed: The nginx settings of the site are not updated, the previous file is kept: {error}
site.ops.vless_not_switched: The VLESS mode was not switched: {error}
site.ops.vless_tls_fell: VLESS did not switch to TLS: {why}. The site is on, VLESS stays on Reality next to it — «Retry TLS»: kaskadctl gw vless mode tls.
site.ops.wait_range: --wait must be a number of seconds from 0 to {max}
site.ops.what.domain_changed: the domain changed, its certificate was removed
site.ops.what.domain_cleared: the domain was removed, the protocol is back on the self-signed certificate and the server’s address
site.ops.what.hy2_cert: Hysteria2 moved to the domain’s certificate: the links have another address and no fingerprint
site.ops.what.use_off: the protocol is back on the self-signed certificate and the server’s address
site.ops.what.use_on: the server address in the settings changes to {domain}, the certificate — to Let’s Encrypt
site.ops.what.vless_cert: VLESS went on TLS with the own domain
site.ops.what.hy2_vless_cert: Hysteria2 and VLESS moved to the domain’s certificate: the links name another address
site.panel.domain: a domain is needed, for example vpn.example.com
site.panel.email: email must be a string (empty — no email)
site.panel.ids: ids must be a list of template numbers
site.panel.ids_max: ids: at most {max} templates at a time (the visible page)
site.panel.kind: kind must be sstp or ocserv
site.panel.mode: mode must be site or domain
site.panel.page: page must be a positive page number
site.panel.template: {field} must be a template number or random
site.panel.wait: wait must be a number of seconds from 0 to {max}
site.tplhealth.gone: Template deleted by its author — can’t be chosen
site.tplhealth.log_cache: SITE: the template check cache was not written: {error}
site.tplhealth.no_preview: The preview was taken down by its author, the template itself installs
site.ops.vless_price_off: The site on the domain will go off, VLESS will switch to Reality (backup) posing as {site}. {short} VLESS links — give them out again (devices — {n}: {who}).
site.ops.vless_price_off_choice: Your choice of Reality with the own site goes away: the own site is off, and a foreign cover site needs a consent of its own. When the site is switched on again, VLESS goes on TLS.
site.ops.vless_price_off_back: To get TLS back, switch the site on again.
site.ops.vless_price_clear_choice: Your choice of Reality with the own site goes away: there is no own site without the domain, and a foreign cover site needs a consent of its own. When the domain is set again and the site is on, you can switch to TLS.
site.ops.vless_price_clear_back: To get TLS back, set the domain again, issue its certificate and turn the site on.
site.ops.vless_need_pick: Pick the cover site first (gw vless masks --check) and pass it: --vless-site <name>.
site.ops.vless_price_tls: The site will go on, VLESS will switch to TLS with your own domain — give the VLESS links out again (devices — {n}: {who}).
site.ops.vless_price_port: The site will go on and take 443, VLESS Reality will move to port {port} — give the VLESS links out again (devices — {n}: {who}).
